newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers reports record profits after year-ago loss.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers reports record profits after year-ago loss.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co., the drug and personal care products maker, Wednesday reported record sales and earnings for the fourth quarter after losing more than $142 million a year ago due to huge charges to cover breast implant litigation and a company-wide restructuring.

The company, whose products range from anti-cancer drugs to over-the-counter pain-killers such as Excedrin and Bufferin, said it earned $716 million, or $1.43 a share, in the latest quarter vs. a loss of $142 million or 28 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues were also higher, at $4.0 billion, compared with $3.7 billion.

Bristol-Myers said it took a loss in last year's fourth quarter because of a charge of $950 million for breast implant litigation and another charge of $310 million for restructuring, which brought job cuts and plant consolidation world-wide.

For the full year, the New York-based company earned $2.85 billion, or $5.68 a share, compared with $1.8 billion, or $3.58 a share, in 1995. Revenues last year climbed to $15.07 billion from $13.77 billion.
Bristol-Myers' stock was up 12.5 cents at $121.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
